title: Legal Is Not Good: A Pre-Registered Benchmark of Low-Cost Language and Decision Models on a New Strategy Game
abstract: arXiv:2611.28713v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Measure Before You Train argued that an agent's decisions should be measured against ground truth, under a protocol fixed in advance, before anyone trains or replaces the model behind them. We carry the method to a second, very different domain, a turn-based strategy game, and ask a deliberately modest question: how well do low-cost agents play under a pre-registered protocol? hexfolk is a minimal two-player 4X game written for this purpose, so no model has seen its rules or positions. A deterministic engine, one agent interface, a referee that never corrects an illegal or late move, and per-decision logs make every game replayable; questions and expected answers were committed before the games, on held-out seeds with mirrored seats and 95% Wilson intervals. Two small open language models (8B and 3B) lose every game to a few-line rule player. Answering in free text they are invalid on 98% of their decisions; constrained to legal moves th

translated_title: 合法不等于优秀：低成本语言与决策模型在新策略游戏上的预注册基准测试
translated_abstract: 《先测量再训练》一文提出，在任何人训练或替换模型之前，智能体的决策应当在一个预先固定的协议下对照真值进行测量。我们将该方法推广到第二个截然不同的领域——回合制策略游戏，并提出一个刻意保守的问题：在预注册协议下，低成本智能体的表现究竟如何？hexfolk 是为此目的专门编写的一个极简双人 4X 游戏，因此没有任何模型见过它的规则或局面。确定性引擎、统一的智能体接口、一个从不纠正非法或迟交着法的裁判，以及逐决策日志，使每一局对局都可复现；问题和预期答案在对局开始前就已预先提交，采用保留的种子、镜像座位和 95% Wilson 置信区间进行评估。两个小型开源语言模型（8B 和 3B）在每局比赛中都输给了一个仅几行代码的规则玩家。以自由文本作答时，它们 98% 的决策无效；当被限制为只能选择合法着法时……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文构建了一个名为 hexfolk 的全新策略游戏及预注册评测协议，结果表明即使被强制只输出合法着法，小型低成本语言模型（8B 和 3B）仍全面败给几行代码的规则玩家，说明“合法”并不等于“下得好”。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces hexfolk, a novel turn-based 4X strategy game with a pre-registered evaluation protocol, and shows that small low-cost language models (8B and 3B) lose every game to a simple rule-based player—even when constrained to legal moves—demonstrating that "legal" does not mean "good".
